items.headline: 31-year-old man shot near Mount Baker McDonald's; no suspects identified
items.blurb: A 31-year-old man was shot Sunday night near a McDonald's in the Mount Baker area of Seattle, and he walked to an address on 25th Avenue South. Seattle Fire medics took him to Harborview Medical Center in stable condition. Seattle police are investigating, and no suspects or arrests were reported.

items.headline: Bite of Seattle shooter still unidentified three months after July shooting
items.blurb: Investigators have not publicly identified the suspect whose gun is linked by ballistic evidence to the July 26 Seattle Center shooting, which left three dead and four wounded, KOMO reported. A teenager was arrested at the scene.

items.headline: Single Shot owner sentenced to 13 months for unpaid payroll taxes
items.blurb: The owner of the Capitol Hill restaurant Single Shot was sentenced in federal court in Seattle to 13 months in prison and ordered to pay $1.4 million in restitution, KOMO reported.

items.headline: One dead in Sunday shooting in Burien; no arrests reported
items.blurb: One person died after a shooting at about 4 a.m. Sunday near First Avenue in Burien, the King County Sheriff's Office said. No arrests had been made as of Monday.

items.headline: Police find 80 shell casings after Haller Lake shooting, no suspects in custody
items.blurb: Investigators recovered 80 shell casings from five firearms after reports of gunfire shortly after 8:15 a.m. Saturday near North 107th Street and Stone Avenue North, police said. No suspects are in custody.

items.headline: SPD warns of callers posing as sheriff's deputies to demand payment over fake warrants
items.blurb: A Seattle man reported a caller posing as a King County sheriff's deputy who demanded a bond payment over fake warrants, police said in an Oct. 22 blotter post.

items.headline: Teen charged in Bite of Seattle shooting released to home detention
items.blurb: A juvenile court judge on Oct. 21 ordered a 15-year-old charged with first-degree assault in the July 26 Bite of Seattle shooting released to electronic home monitoring over prosecutors' objections.

items.headline: Suspect in Broad Street gas station killing arrested in Chicago
items.blurb: U.S. Marshals arrested Michael O'Neal Fleming, 33, in Chicago on Oct. 20, police said. He is charged with first-degree murder in the Oct. 13 shooting of a clerk at a 76 station in the 300 block of Broad Street.

items.headline: Gunman sought after shoplifting turns to robbery at Jefferson Square Safeway
items.blurb: Police are searching for a man who, according to West Seattle Blog, showed a handgun to store security to get away after shoplifting at the Jefferson Square Safeway around 3 p.m. No arrest has been reported.

items.headline: Multi-vehicle crash and diesel spill block northbound I-5 near Michigan St
items.blurb: Three cars and a semi collided on northbound I-5 just north of the S Michigan St exit around 2:55 p.m. Oct. 20, injuring several people and spilling diesel, Seattle Fire said. Two right lanes stayed closed for hours.

items.headline: Crime persists at 12th and Jackson four months after city pledge
items.blurb: Business owners near 12th Ave S and S Jackson St in Little Saigon say drug dealing and disorder continue four months after the mayor announced a targeted crackdown, FOX 13 reported. The city has not released arrest data.

items.headline: Police seek driver who posed as Uber after Pioneer Square bar pickup
items.blurb: A 25-year-old woman told police a man falsely claimed to be her Uber driver outside a 1st Ave S bar on Oct. 10 and drove her to Kent, where she jumped from the car; SPD cameras in the area were not working.

items.headline: Police report no arrests at downtown Seattle No Kings rally
items.blurb: Thousands rallied at Westlake Park Oct. 19 and marched to Seattle Center; police reported no arrests, no property damage and no incidents.

items.headline: Another pre-dawn storefront break-in reported in the Junction
items.blurb: A storefront in the 4500 block of California Ave SW was breached with a thrown object about 4:15 a.m. Oct. 19 and store property was taken, the Westside Seattle crime report said. No arrest was listed.

items.headline: Catalytic converters cut from cars in Morgan Junction carport
items.blurb: Suspects used battery-powered saws on catalytic converters in a carport in the 6500 block of California Ave SW about 2:30 p.m. Oct. 19, then fled in a dark sedan, according to the Westside Seattle crime report.

items.headline: Another night of gunfire rattles the Central District
items.blurb: 911 callers reported shots across several Central District blocks starting around 2:23 a.m. Sunday, including near 21st and E Cherry and 24th and Yesler. No injuries were reported.

items.headline: Man arrested in bed after West Seattle break-in, police say
items.blurb: Police say a 41-year-old man tried to get into one home near Fauntleroy Way SW and SW Webster St on Sunday afternoon, then kicked in the back door of another nearby and was found in a bed there. He was booked for residential burglary and attempted residential burglary.

items.headline: Dangerous CO2 levels force evacuations on Ballard Ave
items.blurb: Seattle Fire hazmat crews found dangerous carbon dioxide levels at a commercial building near the 5400 block of Ballard Ave. Nearby businesses were evacuated as a precaution until the leak was secured. No injuries were reported.

items.headline: Car found half-sunk in Union Bay off East Montlake Park
items.blurb: Before dawn Saturday a vehicle was found partly submerged a few feet from shore near E Shelby St and E Park Dr E. Seattle Fire rescue swimmers searched the water; how it got there was not yet known.

items.headline: Shoplifter shoves worker, flees with designer coats at Westwood Village
items.blurb: A suspect grabbed designer outerwear from a store in the 2600 block of SW Barton St, pushed an employee who intervened and fled, according to the crime report. No arrest was listed.

items.headline: Junction break-ins continue: electronics store and office safe targeted
items.blurb: Burglars smashed into an electronics store in the 4700 block of California Ave SW on Oct. 15 and took devices, then broke into a storefront in the 4500 block on Oct. 17 and tampered with an office safe. No arrests were listed.

items.headline: Hit-and-run driver plows into parked cars on Fauntleroy Way SW
items.blurb: A driver struck parked sedans in the 8800 block of Fauntleroy Way SW Saturday morning and fled the scene, the report says.

items.headline: Suspicious package forces hazmat sweep at Jayapal's downtown office
items.blurb: Hazmat crews checked a suspicious package sent to Rep. Pramila Jayapal's office building in the 2000 block of 6th Ave on Friday. No one was hurt; the FBI is investigating a wave of suspicious mailings to congressional and election offices.

items.headline: Shootout near Garfield sends bullet into 7th-floor apartment hallway
items.blurb: Gunfire broke out Friday night near 23rd Ave and E Jefferson, across from the Garfield Teen Life Center, and a bullet was later found in a seventh-floor hallway of a nearby apartment building. No injuries were reported; police closed the intersection to investigate.

items.headline: SPD lieutenant reprimanded over Cal Anderson rally conduct
items.blurb: After an Office of Police Accountability investigation, Interim Chief Sayles issued a written reprimand to a lieutenant over his conduct during a May 24, 2025 rally and counterdemonstration at Cal Anderson Park.

items.headline: Catalytic converter thief threatens resident who confronts him
items.blurb: A resident in the 4100 block of 26th Ave SW was threatened after interrupting a catalytic converter theft early Oct. 16. The suspect got away.

items.headline: 25 years on, feds say Tom Wales murder is 'not a cold case'
items.blurb: Crime Stoppers says the 2001 shooting of the federal prosecutor in his Queen Anne home remains an active FBI-SPD investigation, with up to $2.5 million offered for information leading to an arrest.

items.headline: Porch pirates strike again on Admiral's 42nd Ave SW
items.blurb: Package thefts were reported from several homes in the 2300 block of 42nd Ave SW; police are tracking a suspect vehicle.

items.headline: Hazmat scare empties a floor of Amazon's Doppler tower
items.blurb: Seattle firefighters evacuated the second floor of the 2000-block 6th Ave high-rise as a precaution after reports of a potentially hazardous substance. No injuries were reported.

items.headline: Man charged in 2024 South Park kidnapping and rape
items.blurb: A 58-year-old man arrested Oct. 8 was charged Oct. 13 with first-degree kidnapping with sexual motivation and second-degree rape over an alleged November 2024 attack in South Park. Previously convicted in Capitol Hill fake-taxi assaults, he could face life without parole if convicted, CHS reports.

items.headline: Armed-man search puts Mount Baker elementary in shelter-in-place
items.blurb: Police searched the 3300 block of S Horton St for a known suspect they believed might be armed and in crisis; nearby John Muir Elementary sheltered in place as a precaution. No arrest was reported.

items.headline: White-powder letter forces partial evacuation of downtown federal building
items.blurb: A suspicious letter with white powder was found Oct. 15 on the 32nd floor of the Henry M. Jackson Federal Building, which houses Sen. Maria Cantwell's offices. Fire crews removed it, no one was hurt, and the FBI is investigating it as part of a nationwide probe of suspicious mailings.

items.headline: Six cars' windows smashed along California Ave SW in Morgan Junction
items.blurb: Someone shattered windows on six vehicles near the 6400 block of California Ave SW the night of Oct. 15 and took items; police later located a person of interest.

items.headline: Alki equipment container broken into; tools recovered
items.blurb: An equipment container in the 2700 block of Alki Ave SW was breached Oct. 15; tools were recovered and a suspect was located, the report says.

items.headline: Rollover crash blocks northbound I-5 near Denny Way
items.blurb: Multiple vehicles collided and one overturned on northbound I-5 near Denny Way Thursday morning; three people were evaluated and reported stable.

items.headline: Suspect tries to set patrol car on fire outside West Precinct, police say
items.blurb: A suspect poured an accelerant on a Seattle police patrol vehicle outside the West Precinct and tried to set it on fire on Oct. 15, according to SPD's significant incident report for that day.

items.headline: Junction smash-and-grab spree: storefronts and a bakery hit
items.blurb: A suspect breached a California Ave SW storefront with a masonry projectile, and a burglar shattered a bakery's front door and tried to pry open its drop-safe, the same day.

items.headline: Two held after package-theft run in North Delridge
items.blurb: Police detained two suspects near SW Barton St and 24th Ave SW who had taken eight packages from five addresses.

items.headline: City Attorney adds prosecutors for Aurora trafficking, gun cases
items.blurb: City Attorney Erika Evans announced two dedicated prosecutors: one cross-deputized to pursue sex-trafficking cases on Aurora Avenue North, and one to lead a new Firearms Unit.

items.headline: Driver trapped after crash on the Ave at NE 42nd St in U District
items.blurb: Seattle Fire crews worked to free a person trapped in a car after a collision at University Way NE and NE 42nd St on the night of Oct. 14; the person's condition was not released.

items.headline: Alki burglar forces patio door, grabs laptops and jewelry
items.blurb: A residential burglar forced a patio door in the 2800 block of 48th Ave SW and stole laptops, jewelry and camera gear.

items.headline: Catalytic converters sawed off three hybrids in Morgan Junction
items.blurb: Thieves cut converters from three parked hybrids in the 6400 block of California Ave SW.

items.headline: Open-air drug market takes root on 2nd Ave in Belltown, owners say
items.blurb: Business owners describe a daytime drug market and sidewalk encampment near 2nd Ave between Bell and Blanchard as the mayor faces questions after a violent weekend.

items.headline: Tools and laser levels stolen from Morgan Junction job site
items.blurb: Padlocks were cut at a construction site in the 6900 block of 35th Ave SW on the afternoon of Oct. 13 and tools and laser levels were taken, the Westside Seattle crime report said.

items.headline: Man stabbed in the head in botched robbery at Woodland Park
items.blurb: A man was stabbed near a picnic shelter around 12:30 a.m. Monday and taken to Harborview with injuries police called not life-threatening. Police believe he knew the suspect; no arrest yet.

items.headline: Masked gunman robs Roxbury convenience store
items.blurb: A masked man with a gun robbed a convenience store in the 1500 block of SW Roxbury St and ran off on foot.

items.headline: Man shot in the stomach in Rainier Beach parking lot
items.blurb: Officers responding to shots fired around 2:30 a.m. found a man about 30 shot in a lot along Rainier Ave S. He was taken to Harborview in critical condition; no arrests.

items.headline: Suspected DUI driver topples power pole on Greenwood Ave N
items.blurb: A 20-year-old driver hit a pole and a building at Greenwood Ave N and N 105th St before 4 a.m. Monday, downing lines and closing the street. He was arrested on suspicion of DUI.

items.headline: Man accused in CID Metro bus machete attack escapes home detention
items.blurb: A 30-year-old man charged over a July 2 machete attack on a Route 7 bus in the Chinatown-International District left electronic home detention without approval; his whereabouts are unknown.

items.headline: Motorcyclist killed under semi on I-5 near S Albro Place
items.blurb: An 18-year-old motorcyclist died Monday after clipping a car while changing lanes on northbound I-5 just north of S Albro Place and going under a semi, the State Patrol says. Lanes were blocked for hours.

items.headline: Drive-by at 4th Ave S nightclub kills security guard, wounds woman
items.blurb: Shortly before 1 a.m. Oct. 11 shots were fired from a vehicle into the lot of a nightclub in the 5800 block of 4th Ave S, killing a 36-year-old security guard and wounding a woman. The car was later found burned in SODO; no arrests. The reward is now $15,000.

items.headline: Burglars pry jewelry store's back door, try for floor safe in Junction
items.blurb: Suspects pried the rear door of a jewelry retailer in the 4500 block of California Ave SW and tried to open a floor safe before fleeing.

items.headline: 50 shell casings: teen arrested after Kerry Park party shooting
items.blurb: Two men were wounded when gunfire broke out at a late-night street party at Kerry Park. Police arrested a juvenile on assault charges after finding a rifle in a vehicle, and collected 50 casings.

items.headline: Pedestrian killed on 15th Ave NW in pre-dawn Ballard crash
items.blurb: A driver called 911 to say he had hit a pedestrian; medics found the person dead in the northbound lanes of 15th Avenue Northwest.

items.headline: Nightlife dispute ends in gunfire on 10th Ave in Pike/Pine
items.blurb: A dispute amid Saturday-night crowds led to shots on 10th Ave between Pike and Union, damaging a window. No injuries were reported.

items.headline: Machete attack at Hing Hay Park: man charged with assault
items.blurb: Prosecutors charged a 44-year-old man with first- and second-degree assault over an Oct. 9 machete attack on two people in the Chinatown-International District park. On Oct. 14 a judge denied his release request, calling him an extreme danger, and kept bail at $500,000.

items.headline: SUV swiped from Fauntleroy ferry line
items.blurb: An unattended SUV was stolen from the ferry queue in the 4800 block of Fauntleroy Way SW and later recovered in Arbor Heights.

items.headline: Trafficking unit sweeps Aurora, makes arrests
items.blurb: More than 20 SPD personnel targeted prostitution solicitation along Aurora Avenue North on Oct. 6; seven men ages 22 to 64 were arrested, several from out of town, Hoodline reported.

items.headline: Cyclist robbed at knifepoint on the Delridge trail
items.blurb: Three people robbed a cyclist at knifepoint near the 3800 block of Delridge Way SW.

items.headline: Cops Tase man accused of hammer threats at 10th and John
items.blurb: Police used pepper balls and a Taser to arrest a man reported to be threatening people with a hammer and machete near 10th Ave and E John St, chasing him into the apartments above Capitol Hill Station.

items.headline: Overheated ceiling fan blamed for Loyal Heights house fire
items.blurb: Firefighters knocked down an attic fire at a home in the 8000 block of 24th Ave NW within 30 minutes Wednesday evening; no one was hurt and investigators ruled it accidental.

items.headline: Shots fired in Aurora gas station lot, man hurt
items.blurb: Detectives are investigating a shooting in a gas station parking lot in the 10500 block of Aurora Avenue North; a 44-year-old man had head injuries possibly from broken glass.

items.headline: Shots fired in High Point, parked car hit
items.blurb: Casings were recovered and a parked sedan was damaged after gunfire in the 6500 block of 35th Ave SW. No one was reported hurt.

items.headline: Hit-and-run leaves cyclist critical; police hunt silver Camry
items.blurb: Detectives say the suspect vehicle is a silver 2012–2014 Toyota Camry sedan. The cyclist remains in critical condition.

items.headline: Man shot twice near 8th Ave NE in Northgate
items.blurb: A 23-year-old man was found with two gunshot wounds in a parking lot near the 11000 block of 8th Ave NE around 12:30 a.m. He was taken to Harborview in stable condition; no arrests.

items.headline: Daytime porch-pirate crew hits Admiral block
items.blurb: A package-theft crew worked the 2300 block of 44th Ave SW in the afternoon.

items.headline: Woman charged in downtown face-biting attack near courthouse
items.blurb: Prosecutors charged a 36-year-old woman with second-degree assault over the Sept. 18 attack near Cherry Street that left another woman with permanent injuries; she was first held on suspicion of a hate crime and says she was the one attacked.

items.headline: Three in dark sedan fire into Rainier Ave S parking lot
items.blurb: Witnesses told police three people in a dark sedan fired rounds into a parking lot in the 4400 block of Rainier Ave S around 10 p.m.

items.headline: Parking officer hit by car while writing ticket on the Ave
items.blurb: Police say a car struck a parking enforcement officer ticketing it in the 4500 block of University Way NE, and the owner jumped in and drove off.

items.headline: Four commuter cars' rear windows smashed at Westwood Village garage
items.blurb: Four vehicles had rear windows broken in a parking structure in the 2600 block of SW Barton St.

items.headline: Police probe report of woman luring kids at Alki Elementary fence
items.blurb: Three first-graders told staff a woman at the playground fence offered to show them a crown in her car. The children ran to an adult, and the woman drove off in a silver vehicle. Seattle police are investigating, and the school has stepped up recess supervision.

items.headline: Family seeks $30M over fatal police shooting behind SW Precinct
items.blurb: Relatives of a man shot by an officer in March 2025 in a lot behind SPD's Southwest Precinct filed a $30 million claim alleging excessive force and negligence. Prosecutors had declined criminal charges.

items.headline: Woman cut, beaten and robbed after getting into car in North Seattle
items.blurb: Police say two men forced a 27-year-old woman out of a car near N 130th St and Greenwood Ave N early Sept. 30 after cutting and punching her and taking her cash. Robbery detectives are investigating.

items.headline: Antisemitic slogans spray-painted on Beer Sheva Park sign
items.blurb: Officers responded to a report of antisemitic graffiti painted on a concrete sign on the park's southwest side.

items.headline: SWAT arrests man accused of hatchet attacks on Greenwood roommate
items.blurb: Police say a 37-year-old man went after his roommate with a hatchet twice at a building in the 8700 block of Greenwood Ave N, then barricaded himself; SWAT took him into custody that evening. The roommate was unhurt.

items.headline: Highland Park pet shop break-in foiled by owner's alarm
items.blurb: An intruder picked a lock and bashed the door of a pet shop in the 800 block of SW Holden St but fled after the owner's alert went off.

items.headline: Shoplifter swings sharp pole at security near the Junction, police say
items.blurb: Police responded to a robbery call in the 4700 block of 42nd Ave SW after a suspected shoplifter swung a long, sharp pole at security staff who confronted him. A K9 team tracked down a possible suspect.

items.headline: Street robbery and beating on SW Roxbury near Delridge
items.blurb: Police took a report of a street robbery and assault in the 1600 block of SW Roxbury St on the evening of Sept. 28. No arrest was reported.

items.headline: Arbor Heights homeowner yells, would-be burglar flees
items.blurb: An intruder broke a sliding window at a home in the 10400 block of 42nd Ave SW but ran when the homeowner shouted.

items.headline: Gunfire, then a crash outside Pioneer Square club
items.blurb: Officers heard shots near the 300 block of 2nd Ave S around 2 a.m., followed by a collision outside a nearby club; occupants reportedly moved items into another vehicle.

items.headline: Burglars haul registers out of Alki ice cream and boba shop
items.blurb: Burglars tried a side door at one Alki Ave SW business, then broke into an ice cream and boba shop in the 2600 block and took two registers and a lockbox.

items.headline: Fuel thieves blamed for SoDo box-truck blaze
items.blurb: Police say two people trying to siphon fuel at a 1st Ave S rental lot sparked the Sept. 25 fire that burned three trucks, causing more than $150,000 in damage. A man first arrested was released; the suspects are still sought.

items.headline: Independent team takes over probe of police-involved death
items.blurb: At SPD's request, the Independent Force Investigative Team – King County is investigating the Sept. 12 death of a man who lost consciousness after being handcuffed on the 6000 block of Airport Way S.

items.headline: Group beats, robs woman in Junction parking lot
items.blurb: Police say four men surrounded a woman in the 4500 block of 42nd Ave SW, took her phone and stomped on her; she was hospitalized. Suspects fled in a white Honda Accord with no plates.

items.headline: Woman critically hurt after Sound Transit train strikes her in SoDo
items.blurb: A 38-year-old woman was struck by a Sound Transit train while crossing the tracks near 2nd Avenue in SoDo, police said. She was hospitalized in critical condition.

items.headline: Meadowbrook house fire injures resident, eight firefighters
items.blurb: A pre-dawn fire that started outside a home in the 12000 block of Sand Point Way NE spread into the house on Sept. 24. A 57-year-old man was taken to Harborview in stable condition; eight firefighters had minor injuries after a carport collapsed on them.

items.headline: Nine firefighters hurt as deck collapses at Sand Point Way NE house fire
items.blurb: A deck partially collapsed during a pre-dawn Sept. 24 fire at a home in the 12000 block of Sand Point Way NE near Matthews Beach, injuring nine firefighters; the cause is under investigation.

items.headline: Arrest after Highland Park stabbing on SW Holden
items.blurb: A person suffered a forearm cut in a stabbing in the 1100 block of SW Holden St; a suspect was arrested and booked.

items.headline: Drive-up gunman shoots man at Rainier Beach encampment
items.blurb: A man about 42 was shot in the chest at an encampment in the 9200 block of 42nd Ave S by someone in a vehicle who fled. He was in stable condition; no arrests.

items.headline: Deputies' PIT maneuver flips stolen car at 1st Ave S and Dawson
items.blurb: King County deputies say a suspected DUI driver in a stolen car with outstanding warrants rolled over after a PIT maneuver near S Dawson St and 1st Ave S; he tried to run and was booked for felony eluding.

items.headline: Masked man implies gun, robs Westwood Village cash counter
items.blurb: A masked man implied he had a gun and demanded cash at a financial-service counter in the 2600 block of SW Barton St, then fled toward 26th Ave SW.

items.headline: Admiral storefronts etched with acid, window cracked by brick
items.blurb: Vandals etched storefront windows with acid and cracked a display window with a thrown brick in the 2300 block of California Ave SW; no one got inside.

items.headline: E-bikes stolen from Morgan Junction garage
items.blurb: A burglar got into a garage through a window in the 6500 block of 44th Ave SW and took two e-bikes and battery packs.

items.headline: Two wounded in Yesler Terrace shooting; teen faces gun charge
items.blurb: A teen shot in the leg on 10th Ave S was found with a loaded handgun and was to be booked on a firearm charge; a second wounded person showed up at Harborview. Both were stable.

items.headline: Man and woman shot dead in car crashed at MLK and Graham
items.blurb: Officers found a car over the curb at MLK Jr. Way S and S Graham St around 2:40 a.m. with a man and a woman shot inside; both died. Homicide detectives are investigating.

items.headline: Hit-and-run driver leaves pedestrian badly hurt on Delridge Way
items.blurb: A northbound dark sedan hit a pedestrian in the crosswalk at Delridge Way SW and SW Brandon St and kept going; the victim went to Harborview with severe fractures.

items.headline: Officer shoots assault suspect in Beacon Hill apartment standoff
items.blurb: After a man was found with a head wound at the Beacon Pacific Village apartments on Golf Dr S, officers entered with a warrant; one fired, wounding the woman suspect, and was hurt. She is in custody; IFIT-KC is investigating.

items.headline: Police hunt man who broke into Maple Leaf home and assaulted a child
items.blurb: Police say a man entered a Maple Leaf home around 5 a.m. Sept. 13 and sexually assaulted a child before leaving. He is described as a white man, 20 to 50, about 200 pounds, last seen in a black hoodie; tips go to 206-233-5000.

items.headline: Late-night gunfire reported on SW Roxbury St
items.blurb: Shots were reported in the 2400 block of SW Roxbury St around 10:50 p.m. Sept. 18. No injuries or arrests were reported.

items.headline: Man, 44, arrested in Sept. 6 Belltown shooting death
items.blurb: Detectives arrested a 44-year-old man on Sept. 14 in connection with the Sept. 6 shooting at 3rd Avenue and Blanchard Street that killed a 23-year-old woman, police said.

items.headline: Man arrested after car set on fire on Hiawatha Place S
items.blurb: Police say a man broke a vehicle window and set the car on fire outside an apartment building in the 800 block of Hiawatha Place S on Sept. 13; witnesses identified him and he was arrested.

items.headline: Rollover crash traps driver, closes westbound West Seattle Bridge
items.blurb: A driver trapped in a rollover near the west end of the westbound West Seattle Bridge on Sunday morning, Sept. 13, was freed by firefighters and reported in stable condition.
